title: Developing an RPG that works on GBA
author: Downtown_Tone_
selftext:
Painstakingly difficult and time consuming and using up a lot of usage. However, I've got to the point now where I've got a  very early alpha build for the battle system, including a basic rotating battle camera, a turn order bar, which actors travel down faster depending on their speed stat, and spells that cut to different backgrounds (which I'll probably use for more spectacular looking summon attacks). 

I'm using Astra Extra high for developing and testing - it seems to use less usage that medium as it's making less mistakes. I'm using Sol medium for research - looking online and having it play and watch GBA games to try and understand how its working. I'm having to watch the screen most of the time to correct decisions and help ensure developments going in the right direction. i then use Asta Extra high to audit the work it does, before updating a 'GBA RPG Core / Framework'.

On the other side, I've had a 30-50 hour story for a game in my head for years. So whilst I'm waiting for my weekly usage to reset I'm nothing down the storyboards, characters, places, world lore, spells and so on, using Milanote.

comments.author: Own_Principle_7901
comments.body: Looks dope. GBA is one of my favorite consoles and it's amazing to see people still building games to it.

comments.author: dazreil
comments.body: If you don’t mind me asking, what did you use to make the graphics?

replies.author: Downtown_Tone_
replies.body: Mainly AI-assisted concept/source art, then it gets converted and tweaked by Astra to work properly as real GBA graphics. Still refining the art pipeline quite a bit - just needed some sprites here to work with when testing the battle system

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body: that generated image to sprite asset pipeline is a pain in the butt, huh?

replies.author: ArachnidConstant8514
replies.body: If you know a better way I would love to know. It is what is holding me back at this point.

comments.author: snakesoul
comments.body: That looks like a real studio game, congrats, it's beautiful. Would you mind sharing the stack used for this please?

replies.author: Downtown_Tone_
replies.body: Thanks! Native GBA ROM in C++ using Butano/devkitARM, with a custom RPG/battle engine on top. I’m using Astra heavily for implementation/testing/auditing whilst directing and playtesting it.

comments.author: Kashmakers
comments.body:
The perspective swap from party members to enemy turn looks so good! The battle camera adds a lot to it.

Playing it on an actual GBA seems fun, too.

replies.author: Downtown_Tone_
replies.body: Thanks! The camera has been one of the hardest bits. I’ve changed between different techniques a few times. Still needs tweaking but looking much better now

comments.author: Professional-Mark283
comments.body: That looks amazing! Crazy Golden Sun vibes. I'm assuming it works on PC as well though right? Would be a shame to just leave it on the GBA!

replies.author: Downtown_Tone_
replies.body:
Yep, it’ll run on PC through a GBA emulator, but it’s being built for the actual 240×160 GBA screen, so if you stretch it fullscreen it’ll look very pixelated — same as most GBA games. 

On, I’m asking for detailed reoorta on usage per each task and so far it seems more efficient for the really hard stuff (like camera rotation) because it gets closer to the right solution first time, but I’m still collecting data.

comments.author: MoonkeyAcid
comments.body: I’m also working on a GBA game! It’s so much fun but also really challenging. Your game is looking awesome.

comments.author: antonation
comments.body: What resources are you using? I imagine there's an SDK for gba development right? Also, happy to see Golden Sun vibes!

replies.author: Downtown_Tone_
replies.body: Yep — I’m using Butano + devkitARM/devkitPro, then building a custom RPG framework on top for battles, camera, UI, world systems, saves, etc

comments.author: FishDeenz
comments.body: That camera swivel is super cool!

comments.author: HugoDzz
comments.body:
That's so cool!! That 2.5D effect is neat. I've been making GBA games as well with Astra. Made a write-up about my process [here](https://www.spritefusion.com/blog/making-a-game-boy-advance-game-with-gpt-6-astra).
